name: The Charted World
summary: The global view: one charted continent, four named waters, and a horizon nobody has returned from. Everything the mapmakers of Velkash dare to draw on a single sheet.

coordinate_convention.note: Every 'map' block in world data uses this grid. The Guild of Charted Lands in Velkash sells a six-foot cloth copy; the edges are deliberately left blank.

charted_landmasses.name: Aurelith
charted_landmasses.summary: The cradle of the mortal realms and the only landmass on any surviving map. Everything else is water, weather, and rumor.

uncharted_rumors.name: The Far Shore
uncharted_rumors.summary: Sailors swear a grey line shows on the southern horizon some dawns. No ship that chased it came back; the Skeleton Courts hold it is the hulls of the drowned standing in a row.

uncharted_rumors.name: Beyond the Pale Main
uncharted_rumors.summary: Ice and silence. Deep-folk saga-keeps say their oldest holds continue under the sea-floor northward, but no living clan claims those doors.

waters.name: The Veiled Sea
waters.summary: The western waters, grey and fog-bound. Ships that sail past the horizon are said to find the Veil itself; the Wealdmark's fishermen work its shelf and no farther. Storm-Bound convoys have twice reported meeting their own wakes sailing the other way.

waters.name: The Pale Main
waters.summary: The cold northern ocean: white water, iceberg fields, and a wind that strips prayer off the tongue. Northmarch's whalers take two weeks of profit a year from its edge and lose a ship most winters.

waters.name: The Bone Sea
waters.position: east of Aurelith, around the Bone Archipelago
waters.summary: The storm-lashed eastern sea, named for the skeleton coasts it gnaws. Reef-charts are worth more than cargo here; the Skeleton Courts sell theirs twice. The Storm-Bound run escort through it and call it an honest sea — it kills you to your face.

waters.name: The Burnt Shallows
waters.summary: A hot, shallow, salt-crusted sea off the desert's south coast. At low tide the flats stink of brine and glass-dust; deep-draft ships must anchor a full day out. Hollowborn salt-gatherers walk the flats at dawn, signing as they work.

notes: Aurelith is the whole of the known world; the seas are its walls and its road.
Sea names are Velkash chart usage; each culture has its own (the Dhar Roads sign 'the dry ring' for all four at once).
